title: A safe share
description: Share the coins without crashing, whatever the player types.

tasks.title: Catch an error before it stops the program
tasks.body: Code inside try: runs as usual. If one of its lines raises an error that an except names, Python jumps to that except block instead of stopping. int("seven") raises a ValueError, so except ValueError: catches it.
tasks.detail: Name the error you expect. A bare except: catches every error, even a typing mistake of your own, and hides it. else: runs when nothing went wrong, and finally: runs either way. Keep the try block short, so you know which lines it protects.

tasks.output:
5
not a number
nobody to share with
tasks.note: Each reply gets its own try. "zero" fails inside int() and jumps to the ValueError block. 0 gets through int() but fails at the division, so the other block catches it.

tasks.question: What would happen with the reply "4.5"?
tasks.why: int() only reads whole numbers, so "4.5" raises a ValueError, which the first except catches.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: add "4.5" and "-3" to the replies. Then take out the ZeroDivisionError block and see what happens to the 0.

Ask how many coins there are, then how many friends share them. Print each friend's share, using //, and then the coins left over, using %. If either reply is not a whole number, print just not a number instead. If there are 0 friends, print just nobody to share with instead.
tasks.starter: # Read both replies, and share the coins safely
hints: Put the lines that can fail, the two int() calls and the sharing, inside one try: block.
Add one except block for each kind of error you expect: a reply that is not a whole number, and a share among 0 friends. Each one prints its own message.
With other names: try: with n = int(reply) inside it, then except ValueError: with print("try again") inside that.

error_hints.text: int() could not read a reply. Put the int() lines inside try:, and add an except ValueError: block.
Sharing among 0 friends raises a ZeroDivisionError. Catch it with an except block of its own.
The lines inside try: and inside each except: start with four spaces.
With 60 coins and 7 friends, each gets 8 and 4 are left over.
When the coins are typed as a word, the program prints only not a number.
With 0 friends the program prints only nobody to share with, and no share.
Check a number of friends that is not a whole number.
Check a number of coins with a decimal point: int() refuses it.

similar_example.note: One kind of error caught for two replies. Your share needs two except blocks, because two different things can go wrong.

other_ways.note: else: runs only when the try block raised nothing, so the printing is kept apart from the lines that can fail.
An if can check for 0 before dividing. try suits errors you cannot easily check first, like text that may not be a number.
